com.github.MitjaNemec.PlaceFootprints.note: Runs here. Select one footprint first; the others are lined up, put in a grid or on a circle from it.

com.github.MitjaNemec.ReplicateLayout.note: Runs here. Select one footprint of the sheet that is laid out; the other sheets' parts, tracks and zones follow it. Locked footprints stay where they are unless you tick the box.

com.github.MitjaNemec.SaveRestoreLayout.note: Runs here. Save gives you the layout file as a download; Restore asks you to pick that file and lays the selected sheet out from it.

com.github.MitjaNemec.SwapStubs.note: It opens and its window responds, but its result has not been checked here yet: the earlier check only saw the plugin's own log or settings file.

com.github.Sajitha-Aldeniya.KiCAD-Schema.note: Runs here. Copy in the schematic editor, then Save Block; Import puts a block back in the editor's copy buffer for Paste. Blocks are kept with the project in this browser.

com.github.Steffen-W.impartGUI.note: Runs here. A part imported by its LCSC number comes as a symbol library and a footprint, which the editor offers to add to the project's libraries. A vendor's part ZIP is imported by dropping it on the plugin's window, since there is no Downloads folder to watch. Checked with a recorded answer from EasyEDA, not the live service; the 3D model was not in that recording. Needs network access granted.

com.github.SteveMayze.pcb2fritzing.note: Give it an output folder name; the Fritzing part comes as a download. Its optional 3D picture is drawn by the editor's 3D viewer.

com.github.adamws.kicad-git.note: Its button opens the Save Version dialog. The project's version history stands in for git here: a commit is a saved version.

com.github.adamws.kicad-kbplacer.note: It opens and its window responds, but its result has not been checked here yet: the earlier check only saw the plugin's own log or settings file.

com.github.aivon-pcba.aivon-plug-in-for-.note: Runs here. What it sends was checked against a stand-in for the vendor's service built from the plugin's own code, not against the live service: the upload holds the Gerbers, drill files, netlist and part lists with the board's size and layer count, and the quote page it names is opened. Needs network access granted.

com.github.bbenchoff.orthoroute.note: Its button runs, but its window is built with PyQt6, which the web editor does not have, so the router window does not open.

com.github.black-ghost-off.autoled.note: Placing LEDs, capacitors and connectors from a picture works, with the footprints of KiCad's own libraries. Its autorouting step starts Freerouting, a Java program, which a browser cannot run: route the result with the editor's own router.

com.github.danielboston38.prefab-gate.note: Its check runs on the web editor's Design Rules Checker, which covers fewer rules than KiCad's desktop DRC. Zones are refilled first by the web editor's own filler. Read a pass as a first check, not as KiCad's verdict.

com.github.drandyhaas.kicadroutingtools.note: It loads with its compiled packages (numpy, shapely and the like) and opens, but its result has not been checked here with its main button pressed.

com.github.drewsum.kipi.note: Its Qt window and its numpy, scipy and matplotlib parts load. Its solver meshes the copper with the Triangle library, which is compiled code that has no build for the browser.

com.github.f-blaze.velatrace.note: Its window opens and its own router routes the board and draws the preview. Its approval step checks the route with the web editor's Design Rules Checker, which covers fewer rules than KiCad's desktop DRC, and its optional Freerouting engine needs Java on a computer.

com.github.fablabkerala.gerber2png-plugi.note: It makes the Gerber archive and hands it over as a download. The Gerber2Png page fetches the archive from a port on your own computer, which a browser tab cannot open: load the downloaded archive in that page instead.

com.github.g200kg.kicad-gerberzipper2.note: Gerbers, drill files, BOM, position file and the ZIP are made. Its optional fabrication PDF step is skipped: PDF plots from kicad-cli are not available to plugins here yet.

com.github.gauravmm.hierarchicalpcb.note: It opens and its window responds, but its result has not been checked here yet: the earlier check only saw the plugin's own log or settings file.

com.github.heronitec-solutions.kicomlib.note: It opens. It keeps library folders on a computer in step with a KiComLib server you run yourself; the web editor has no such folders and a plugin here can only reach the web addresses its own package names.

com.github.jOaSbA.localize-dependencies.note: It opens and reads the project's library tables, but finds nothing to do: an online project already holds its own libraries, and KiCad's standard libraries are served by the editor.

com.github.jarrettr.stretch.note: It opens and its window responds, but its result has not been checked here yet: the earlier check only saw the plugin's own log or settings file.

com.github.mrcpuddington.kobeestudio.note: Runs here. Place artwork puts the label on the board as a footprint that follows the cursor until you click; with an artwork selected the window opens on it and Update artwork replaces it in place.

com.github.officialdyray.projectinstance.note: It opens and its window responds, but its result has not been checked here yet: the earlier check only saw the plugin's own log or settings file.

com.github.pcbway.PCBWay-Plug-in-for-Kic.note: Runs here. What it sends was checked against a stand-in for the vendor's service built from the plugin's own code, not against the live service: the upload holds the Gerbers, drill files, netlist and part lists with the board's size and layer count, and the order page it names is opened. Needs network access granted.

com.github.riehlies.kisi.note: It builds its viewer page for the open board and hands it over as a download; open the downloaded page in your browser.

com.github.samuelcicuitstudio.traceforge.note: Its helper and its panel both run in the page and talk over a local port that stays inside the page. The first launch sets its net highlight shortcut and asks to be opened again, as on the desktop. Signal paths, export, rotation, via and trace tools, net colours and manufacturing checks work. Stitching, fences and rounded corners need the shapely package. Teardrops drive KiCad's own Windows dialog, on the desktop too, and are not available here.

com.github.spice-projects.kicad-xyce-plu.note: It adds no board editor command.

com.github.usetraces.traces.note: It is a client for the traces server (traces-serve), which is installed separately from its own source and is not part of this package. A plugin here cannot reach a server on your own computer.

com.github.weirdgyn.viastitcher.note: Vias are placed over the zone's filled copper. It keeps its settings per zone on a layer it renames; the editor does not follow a layer rename from a plugin, so it opens with its default settings each time.

com.github.z2labs.eagle-exhumer.note: It imports an Eagle project by starting the KiCad desktop program and pressing its menus through the computer's window system. A browser page cannot start or steer another program.

com.github.z2labs.z2ems.note: Its windows open and the setup is saved. Simulating needs the Z2 EMS engine, a desktop program.

com.gitlab.dennevi.Board2Pdf.note: It loads with its compiled packages (numpy, shapely and the like) and opens, but its result has not been checked here with its main button pressed.

com.gitlab.egloff-studio.z0-field-solver.note: It solves boards whose signal layers lie close to a plane (a four-layer stackup with 0.1 mm prepreg: its 50 ohm width agrees with the textbook formula). A thick two-layer board (1.5 mm core) makes a mesh of over a million cells, and solving that needs more memory than a browser tab gives: it reports a memory error there.

com.gitlab.egloff-studio.z0-wavelab.note: Net check, Monte Carlo and the wave simulation's numbers and pictures are checked. Its Monte Carlo and wave tabs use the same field solver as Z0 Field Solver, so a thick two-layer board can run out of browser memory there.

com.gitlab.open-hardware-designs.kicad-e.note: The panel is checked in full. The stencil Gerbers are drawn by the web editor's own Gerber writer.

com.infernoembedded.vulcans-trials.note: The package holds only a launcher for the vulcans-trials program, a compiled desktop application that is installed separately. Without it the plugin reports that it cannot find the program, on the desktop too.

com.pcbtools.kinotes.note: Notes and tasks are kept per project in this browser, for you only; collaborators do not see them.

com.stenchill.kicad.note: Runs here. What it sends was checked against a stand-in for the vendor's service built from the plugin's own code, not against the live service: the paste and outline Gerbers go up with the stencil settings, the progress stream is followed, the mesh files are saved in a dated folder and handed over, and View in 3D opens the shared page. Needs network access granted.

sierra.kicad.order.note: It runs. What it sends to a web service goes through this server once you grant it network access; the test machine has no network, so that part is untested.
